seo_title: Cost of Living in Bukhara 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Bukhara per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: An ancient Silk Road city with 60 days visa-free entry and some of the lowest prices around. Russian is used in everyday life and the climate is warm, but the pace is provincial and the infrastructure modest.
pros: 60 days visa-free, with Russian used in everyday life
Some of the lowest prices for housing and food
The atmosphere of a living Silk Road, with UNESCO monuments
A warm, dry climate and cheap fruit
Simple registration and a friendly attitude towards Russians
cons: A provincial pace and few international services
Modest IT infrastructure and job market
Few direct flights — usually via Tashkent

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 60 days without a visa — all you need is a passport.

visa_steps.title: Registration
visa_steps.description: If you stay longer than 15 days, arrange a temporary registration at your place of residence.

visa_steps.title: Renting a home
visa_steps.description: Houses and flats rent cheaply; the lease is the basis for registration.

visa_steps.title: Account and card
visa_steps.description: Kapitalbank or Hamkorbank — they issue UZCARD/Humo and Visa cards to Russians with a passport.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit (optional)
visa_steps.description: Through work, property or family reunification, at the migration department of the Interior Ministry.

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Bukhara?
faq.answer: No, up to 60 days visa-free. For stays longer than 15 days, a temporary registration is required.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Bukhara?
faq.answer: Very cheap — one of the most budget-friendly options, cheaper than Tashkent and Samarkand. See the calculator above for an exact budget.

faq.question: What language is spoken in Bukhara?
faq.answer: Uzbek and Tajik; Russian is understood in everyday life, especially by the older generation.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Bukhara?
faq.answer: The MIR card is accepted only in limited places; a local UZCARD/Humo or Visa card is more reliable.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Bukhara?
faq.answer: Sharply continental and desert-like: hot, dry summers up to +40 and cool winters.

faq.question: How do I get to Bukhara?
faq.answer: Most often via Tashkent (a domestic flight or the high-speed Afrosiyob train); there are seasonal direct flights.

reviews.text: Bukhara is a time machine with dirt-cheap prices. I rented a house for next to nothing and work remotely. The downside — it's provincial and there's little IT environment.
I moved for the quiet, the warmth and the history. People understand Russian and are kind, and the food is tasty and cheap. I just miss the big-city services.
